records.source: דִּבְרֵ֥י נְחֶמְיָ֖ה בֶּן־חֲכַלְיָ֑ה וַיְהִ֤י בְחֹֽדֶשׁ־כִּסְלֵיו֙ שְׁנַ֣ת עֶשְׂרִ֔ים וַאֲנִ֥י הָיִ֖יתִי בְּשׁוּשַׁ֥ן הַבִּירָֽה׃
records.gloss: [The] words of Nehemiah son of Hacaliah. And it was in [the] month [of] Kislev, [in the] year twenty, and I was in Susa the citadel.
pieces: The account of Nehemiah son of Hacaliah. In the month of Kislev, in the twentieth year, I was in the citadel of Susa.

L.1: The words of Nehemiah son of Hacaliah. And it came about in the month of Kislev, in the twentieth year, that I was in Susa the citadel.

R.1: This is the account of Nehemiah son of Hacaliah. In the month of Kislev, in the twentieth year that King Artaxerxes ruled, I was in the royal fortress in Susa.

decisions.choice: the words of Nehemiah: the account Nehemiah gives, the heading of the book
decisions.reason: The same opening heads the books of Jeremiah and Amos (Jeremiah 1:1; Amos 1:1). Much of what follows is Nehemiah's own first-person account (chapters 1-7 and 12:31-13:31), so the heading names him as its source.

decisions.choice: Kislev in the twentieth year: the ninth month, about November-December, in the twentieth year of King Artaxerxes
decisions.reason: Kislev is the Babylonian name of the ninth month, used by the Jews after the exile (Zechariah 7:1). The year is counted from the reign of Artaxerxes, named in 2:1; Artaxerxes I ruled Persia from 465 to 424 BC, so this is 445 BC. Nisan, the first month, comes later in the same twentieth year (2:1), which suggests the years of the reign were counted from the autumn.

decisions.choice: Susa the citadel: the fortified royal city of Susa, a residence of the Persian kings
decisions.reason: Susa, in what is now southwest Iran, was one of the capitals of the Persian kings, where they spent the winter. The word for "citadel" names a fortress or palace complex, as in Esther 1:2 and Daniel 8:2.

decisions.choice: the twentieth year that King Artaxerxes ruled
decisions.reason: Readable names the king now, from 2:1, so the reader knows whose reign the year counts.

records.heading: News of Jerusalem reaches Nehemiah in Susa

records.source: וַיָּבֹ֨א חֲנָ֜נִי אֶחָ֧ד מֵאַחַ֛י ה֥וּא וַאֲנָשִׁ֖ים מִֽיהוּדָ֑ה וָאֶשְׁאָלֵ֞ם עַל־הַיְּהוּדִ֧ים הַפְּלֵיטָ֛ה אֲשֶֽׁר־נִשְׁאֲר֥וּ מִן־הַשֶּׁ֖בִי וְעַל־יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃
records.gloss: And came Hanani, one of my brothers, he and men from Judah, and I asked them about the Jews, the escaped who remained from the captivity, and about Jerusalem.
pieces: Hanani, one of my brothers, came with some men from Judah. I asked them about the Jews who had escaped, those who had survived the captivity, and about Jerusalem.

L.2: And Hanani, one of my brothers, came, he and some men from Judah. And I asked them about the Jews who had escaped, who had survived the captivity, and about Jerusalem.

R.2: Hanani, one of my brothers, came with some men from Judah. I asked them how the Jews there were doing, the ones who had survived the exile. I also asked them about Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: one of my brothers: Hanani is most likely Nehemiah's own brother
decisions.reason: The word can mean a relative or a fellow Jew, but in 7:2 Nehemiah calls Hanani "my brother", which points to a brother by birth.

decisions.choice: the escaped who remained from the captivity: the Jews who had survived the exile and now lived in Judah
decisions.reason: The two words, "the escaped" and "who remained", are the language of a remnant that came through a disaster alive (Ezra 9:8, 13-15). Here they name the Jewish community in Judah after the Babylonian captivity, most of them people who had returned from it (Ezra 1-2).

decisions.choice: the exile
decisions.reason: Readable says "exile", the common word for the time when the people were taken away to Babylon.

records.source: וַיֹּאמְרוּ֮ לִי֒ הַֽנִּשְׁאָרִ֞ים אֲשֶֽׁר־נִשְׁאֲר֤וּ מִן־הַשְּׁבִי֙ שָׁ֣ם בַּמְּדִינָ֔ה בְּרָעָ֥ה גְדֹלָ֖ה וּבְחֶרְפָּ֑ה וְחוֹמַ֤ת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ מְפֹרָ֔צֶת וּשְׁעָרֶ֖יהָ נִצְּת֥וּ בָאֵֽשׁ׃
records.gloss: And they said to me, the remaining who remained from the captivity there in the province [are] in great trouble and in disgrace, and [the] wall of Jerusalem [is] broken down and its gates have been burned with fire.
pieces: They said to me, "The survivors of the captivity who are there in the province are in great trouble and disgrace. The wall of Jerusalem is broken down, and its gates have been burned."

L.3: And they said to me, "The remnant who survived the captivity there in the province are in great trouble and disgrace, and the wall of Jerusalem is broken down, and its gates have been burned with fire."

R.3: They told me, "The people who survived the exile and are back in the province of Judah are in serious trouble. Others treat them with scorn. The wall of Jerusalem has been broken down, and its gates have been burned."

decisions.choice: the province: Judah, a small province of the Persian empire
decisions.reason: After the exile Judah was governed as a province of the Persian empire (Ezra 2:1; 5:8), part of the larger region Beyond the River (2:7).

decisions.choice: the wall broken down and the gates burned: Jerusalem lay without defenses
decisions.reason: The Babylonians broke down Jerusalem's walls and burned the city in 586 BC (2 Kings 25:9-10). The news may also include a more recent setback: under this same Artaxerxes the Jews' work on the walls had been stopped by force (Ezra 4:12, 21-23). The text does not say which; either way the city could not be defended.

decisions.choice: disgrace: open shame, being mocked by others
decisions.reason: The word means reproach or scorn from others. A city without walls was a mark of weakness and of God's judgment, and the neighbors mock it (2:17, 19; 3:33-36).

decisions.choice: the province of Judah; Others treat them with scorn
decisions.reason: Readable names the province and says who causes the disgrace, so the reader sees it is shame before others.

records.source: וַיְהִ֞י כְּשָׁמְעִ֣י׀אֶת־הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֗לֶּה יָשַׁ֨בְתִּי֙ וָֽאֶבְכֶּ֔ה וָאֶתְאַבְּלָ֖ה יָמִ֑ים וָֽאֱהִ֥י צָם֙ וּמִתְפַּלֵּ֔ל לִפְנֵ֖י אֱלֹהֵ֥י הַשָּׁמָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And it was, when I heard the words, these, I sat and wept and mourned days, and I was fasting and praying before [the] God of the heavens.
pieces: When I heard these words, I sat down and wept. For some days I mourned, and I kept fasting and praying before the God of heaven.

L.4: And when I heard these words, I sat down and wept and mourned for days, and I was fasting and praying before the God of heaven.

R.4: When I heard this news, I sat down and cried. For several days I was full of grief. I went without food, and I prayed to the God of heaven.

decisions.choice: sat, wept, mourned, fasted: the signs of grief and repentance
decisions.reason: Sitting on the ground, weeping and fasting were how grief and repentance were shown (Ezra 9:3-5; 10:6; Job 2:13). Nehemiah's prayer that follows is also a confession (verses 6-7).

decisions.choice: days: for a number of days
decisions.reason: The plural without a number means "some days". From Kislev (1:1) to Nisan (2:1) is about four months, and the prayer may have gone on through that time (verse 6, "day and night").

decisions.choice: the God of heaven: a title of God common in the Persian period
decisions.reason: The title is used in Cyrus's decree and in the Persian letters (Ezra 1:2; 7:12), and by Nehemiah in his prayers and speech (1:5; 2:4, 20). It names the God of Israel as the God over all.

records.source: וָאֹמַ֗ר אָֽנָּ֤א יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם הָאֵ֥ל הַגָּד֖וֹל וְהַנּוֹרָ֑א שֹׁמֵ֤ר הַבְּרִית֙ וָחֶ֔סֶד לְאֹהֲבָ֖יו וּלְשֹׁמְרֵ֥י מִצְוֺתָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And I said, please, YHWH, God of the heavens, the God, the great and the awesome, keeping the covenant and steadfast love for those loving him and for those keeping his commandments,
pieces: And I said, "Please, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, God of heaven, the great and awesome God, who keeps the covenant and faithful love with those who love {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and keep {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commandments,

L.5: And I said, "Please, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, God of the heavens, the great and awesome God, keeping the covenant and steadfast love with those who love {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and keep {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commandments,

R.5: I said, "Please, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, God of heaven, great and awesome God! You keep {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} covenant and show faithful love to those who love {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} and obey {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} commands.

decisions.choice: the great and awesome God who keeps the covenant and steadfast love: the words of Deuteronomy
decisions.reason: The prayer opens with Moses' words in Deuteronomy 7:9, 21 ("the faithful God, who keeps the covenant and steadfast love with those who love him and keep his commandments"), as Daniel's prayer does (Daniel 9:4). Nehemiah appeals to what God has already said about himself.

decisions.choice: steadfast love: loyal, lasting love that keeps faith with a covenant
decisions.reason: The word means kindness that is owed and freely kept, the love that holds to a relationship. Here it is joined to "covenant", the bond God made with Israel.

decisions.choice: awesome: to be feared, inspiring awe
decisions.reason: The word comes from the verb "to fear". It describes God as one to be held in awe and reverence (Deuteronomy 7:21; 10:17).

decisions.choice: steadfast love (Literal); faithful love (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As elsewhere in the project, Literal says "steadfast love" and Balanced and Readable "faithful love".

decisions.choice: You keep your covenant ... those who love you
decisions.reason: Readable turns the description into a sentence spoken to God, as the prayer goes on to speak to him directly.

records.source: תְּהִ֣י נָ֣א אָזְנְךָֽ־קַשֶּׁ֣בֶת וְֽעֵינֶ֪יךָ פְתֻוּח֟וֹתלִשְׁמֹ֣עַ אֶל־תְּפִלַּ֣ת עַבְדְּךָ֡ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אָנֹכִי֩ מִתְפַּלֵּ֨ל לְפָנֶ֤יךָ הַיּוֹם֙ יוֹמָ֣ם וָלַ֔יְלָה עַל־בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל עֲבָדֶ֑יךָ וּמִתְוַדֶּ֗ה עַל־חַטֹּ֤אות בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָטָ֣אנוּ לָ֔ךְ וַאֲנִ֥י וּבֵית־אָבִ֖י חָטָֽאנוּ׃
records.gloss: let be, please, your ear attentive and your eyes open, to hear [the] prayer of your slave which I [am] praying before you today, by day and night, for [the] sons of Israel your slaves, and confessing the sins of [the] sons of Israel which we have sinned against you; and I and [the] house of my father have sinned.
pieces: let {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} ear be attentive and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} eyes open to hear the prayer of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant, which I pray before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} now, day and night, for the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servants. I confess the sins of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, which we have committed against {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. I and my father's family have sinned.

L.6: let {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} ear be attentive and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} eyes open, to hear the prayer of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} slave which I am praying before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} today, day and night, for the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} slaves, confessing the sins of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel which we have sinned against {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. Both I and my father's house have sinned.

R.6: Please listen and look with care, and hear the prayer that I, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant, am praying to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. Day and night I pray for the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, who are {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servants. I confess the sins that we Israelites have done against {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. I and my own family have sinned too.

decisions.choice: let your ear be attentive and your eyes open: please listen and take notice
decisions.reason: Ear and eyes picture God paying attention to the one who prays, as in Solomon's prayer at the temple (1 Kings 8:29, 52; 2 Chronicles 6:40).

decisions.choice: today, day and night: the prayer he prays now, and has kept praying without stopping
decisions.reason: "Today" points to the prayer he is speaking; "day and night" says he has prayed this way continually, through the days of verse 4.

decisions.choice: confessing the sins of Israel, including his own and his family's
decisions.reason: Nehemiah does not blame others only: he counts himself and his family among those who sinned, as Ezra and Daniel do in their prayers (Ezra 9:6-7; Daniel 9:5-8, 20).

decisions.choice: your slave, your slaves: one who belongs to God and serves him
decisions.reason: Calling oneself God's slave or servant is the humble language of prayer (1 Samuel 3:9-10; 1 Kings 8:28). It speaks of belonging to God and being bound to obey him.

decisions.choice: slave (Literal); servant (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The project's rule for this word: Literal keeps "slave", Balanced and Readable say "servant", since the point here is belonging and service, not slavery itself.

decisions.choice: my father's family (Balanced); my own family (Readable)
decisions.reason: "House of my father" means one's family or clan. Balanced and Readable say "family", as the project does for this phrase.

records.source: חֲבֹ֖ל חָבַ֣לְנוּ לָ֑ךְ וְלֹא־שָׁמַ֣רְנוּ אֶת־הַמִּצְוֺ֗ת וְאֶת־הַֽחֻקִּים֙ וְאֶת־הַמִּשְׁפָּטִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוִּ֖יתָ אֶת־מֹשֶׁ֥ה עַבְדֶּֽךָ׃
records.gloss: Corruptly we have acted corruptly against you, and not we have kept the commandments and the statutes and the judgments which you commanded Moses your slave.
pieces: We have acted very wickedly against {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. We have not kept the commandments, the statutes and the rulings that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} gave to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant Moses.

L.7: We have acted very corruptly against {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, and we have not kept the commandments and the statutes and the judgments which {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} commanded Moses {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} slave.

R.7: We have done what is very wrong against {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. We have not obeyed the commands, laws and rules that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} gave to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant Moses.

decisions.choice: corruptly we have acted corruptly: we have acted very corruptly
decisions.reason: The verb is doubled (an infinitive before the finite verb), which makes it emphatic. The verb means to act in a ruinous, destructive way.

decisions.choice: the commandments, the statutes and the judgments: the whole law given through Moses
decisions.reason: The three words together name all that God commanded in the law (Deuteronomy 5:31; 6:1). Israel's failure to keep it is why the exile came (Deuteronomy 28:15, 64).

decisions.choice: commandments, statutes, judgments (Literal); commandments, statutes, rulings (Balanced); commands, laws, rules (Readable)
decisions.reason: The project's settled wording for these three words of the law.

records.source: זְכָר־נָא֙ אֶת־הַדָּבָ֔ר אֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוִּ֛יתָ אֶת־מֹשֶׁ֥ה עַבְדְּךָ֖ לֵאמֹ֑ר אַתֶּ֣ם תִּמְעָ֔לוּ אֲנִ֕י אָפִ֥יץ אֶתְכֶ֖ם בָּעַמִּֽים׃
records.gloss: Remember, please, the word which you commanded Moses your slave, saying, you, you will act unfaithfully, I, I will scatter you among the peoples;
pieces: Please remember the word that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} gave to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant Moses: 'If you are unfaithful, I will scatter you among the nations.

L.8: Remember, please, the word which {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} commanded Moses {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} slave, saying, 'If you act unfaithfully, I will scatter you among the peoples.

R.8: Please remember what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} told {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant Moses. You said, 'If you are not faithful to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, I will scatter you among the nations.

decisions.choice: the word to Moses: a summary of the warnings and promises of the law
decisions.reason: Nehemiah does not quote one verse but sums up what God said through Moses: unfaithfulness would bring scattering among the nations (Leviticus 26:33; Deuteronomy 4:25-27; 28:64), and turning back would bring gathering (verse 9).

decisions.choice: you will act unfaithfully, I will scatter you: if you are unfaithful, I will scatter you
decisions.reason: The two clauses stand side by side with no "if", but the first states a condition and the second its result, as verse 9 goes on with "and if you return". The pronouns "you" and "I" are written out for emphasis.

decisions.choice: act unfaithfully: break faith, betray a trust
decisions.reason: The verb means to be disloyal to one to whom loyalty is owed, often of turning from God (Leviticus 26:40; Ezra 9:2, 4).

decisions.choice: nations
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "nations", the sense of "peoples" here, foreign peoples outside Israel.

decisions.choice: not faithful to me
decisions.reason: Readable says to whom the faithfulness was owed, which the verb implies.

records.source: וְשַׁבְתֶּ֣ם אֵלַ֔י וּשְׁמַרְתֶּם֙ מִצְוֺתַ֔י וַעֲשִׂיתֶ֖ם אֹתָ֑ם אִם־יִהְיֶ֨ה נִֽדַּחֲכֶ֜ם בִּקְצֵ֤ה הַשָּׁמַ֨יִם֙ מִשָּׁ֣ם אֲקַבְּצֵ֔ם וַהֲבִֽיאוֹתִים֙ אֶל־הַמָּק֔וֹם אֲשֶׁ֣ר בָּחַ֔רְתִּי לְשַׁכֵּ֥ן אֶת־שְׁמִ֖י שָֽׁם׃
records.gloss: and you will return to me and keep my commandments and do them, if will be your banished one at [the] end of the heavens, from there I will gather them and I will bring them to the place which I have chosen to make dwell my name there.
pieces: But if you return to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} commandments and obey them, even if your exiles are at the farthest edge of the sky, I will gather them from there and bring them to the place I have chosen as a dwelling for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name.'

L.9: But if you return to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} commandments and do them, even if your banished ones are at the end of the heavens, from there I will gather them and bring them to the place which I have chosen to make {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name dwell there.'

R.9: But if you come back to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and obey {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} commands, I will gather your people again, even if they have been scattered to the farthest places on earth. I will bring them back to the place I chose, where I will be worshiped.'

decisions.choice: if you return ... even at the end of the heavens, I will gather them: Deuteronomy 30:1-4
decisions.reason: This takes up Moses' promise that if the scattered people turn back to God, he will gather them "even if your banished ones are at the end of the heavens" (Deuteronomy 30:4).

decisions.choice: the end of the heavens: the farthest horizon, the most distant places
decisions.reason: The sky seems to meet the earth at the horizon, so its "end" is the farthest place one can think of (Deuteronomy 4:32; Psalm 19:7).

decisions.choice: the place I have chosen to make my name dwell: Jerusalem and its temple
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy speaks of the place God would choose "to make his name dwell there" (Deuteronomy 12:5, 11). God's name stands for his presence among his people; the place came to be Jerusalem (1 Kings 8:29; 11:36).

decisions.choice: But if you return
decisions.reason: The "and" that joins this to verse 8 turns the warning into its opposite, so Balanced and Readable say "But" and the "if" that the sense needs.

decisions.choice: where I will be worshiped
decisions.reason: Readable says what it means for God's name to dwell in a place, since the picture is not plain to a new reader. It is a simplification: the phrase also speaks of God's presence there.

records.source: וְהֵ֥ם עֲבָדֶ֖יךָ וְעַמֶּ֑ךָ אֲשֶׁ֤ר פָּדִ֨יתָ֙ בְּכֹחֲךָ֣ הַגָּד֔וֹל וּבְיָדְךָ֖ הַחֲזָקָֽה׃
records.gloss: And they [are] your slaves and your people, whom you redeemed by your power, the great, and by your hand, the strong.
pieces: They are {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servants and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people, whom {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} redeemed by {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} great power and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} strong hand.

L.10: And they are {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} slaves and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people, whom {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} redeemed by {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} great power and by {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} strong hand.

R.10: They are {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servants, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} own people. You set them free by {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} great power and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} strong hand.

decisions.choice: your people whom you redeemed by your great power and strong hand: Moses' prayer and the exodus
decisions.reason: Moses prayed in almost these words when Israel had sinned: "they are your people ... whom you brought out by your great power" (Deuteronomy 9:29; Exodus 32:11). The redemption is the rescue from Egypt (Deuteronomy 7:8).

decisions.choice: redeemed: set free, rescued at a price
decisions.reason: The verb means to ransom or set free, used of God bringing Israel out of slavery in Egypt (Deuteronomy 7:8; 15:15).

decisions.choice: strong hand: God's power shown in action
decisions.reason: A strong hand pictures power at work; it is a set phrase for the exodus (Exodus 3:19; Deuteronomy 6:21).

decisions.choice: set them free
decisions.reason: Readable says what "redeemed" means here, freedom from slavery in Egypt.

records.source: אָנָּ֣א אֲדֹנָ֗י תְּהִ֣י נָ֣א אָזְנְךָֽ־קַ֠שֶּׁבֶת אֶל־תְּפִלַּ֨ת עַבְדְּךָ֜ וְאֶל־תְּפִלַּ֣ת עֲבָדֶ֗יךָ הַֽחֲפֵצִים֙ לְיִרְאָ֣ה אֶת־שְׁמֶ֔ךָ וְהַצְלִֽיחָה־נָּ֤א לְעַבְדְּךָ֙ הַיּ֔וֹם וּתְנֵ֣הוּ לְרַחֲמִ֔ים לִפְנֵ֖י הָאִ֣ישׁ הַזֶּ֑ה וַאֲנִ֛י הָיִ֥יתִי מַשְׁקֶ֖ה לַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃פ
records.gloss: Please, my Lord, let be, please, your ear attentive to [the] prayer of your slave and to [the] prayer of your slaves, the ones delighting to fear your name, and give success, please, to your slave today, and give him compassion before the man, this. And I was cupbearer to the king.
pieces: Please, Lord, let {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} ear be attentive to the prayer of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant and to the prayer of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servants who delight to honor {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name. Give {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant success today, and grant him mercy in the sight of this man." Now I was cupbearer to the king.

L.11: Please, my Lord, let {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} ear be attentive to the prayer of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} slave and to the prayer of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} slaves who delight to fear {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name, and give success, please, to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} slave today, and grant him compassion before this man." And I was cupbearer to the king.

R.11: Please, Lord, listen to my prayer. Listen to the prayers of all {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servants who are glad to honor {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. Help me today, and make the king kind to me." At that time I served the king as his cupbearer.

decisions.choice: my Lord: Adonai, a title meaning master, used in address to God
decisions.reason: This is not the divine name of verse 5 but the title "Lord", in the form used only of God.

decisions.choice: delight to fear your name: gladly revere God
decisions.reason: To fear God's name is to hold him in awe and honor, which shows in obeying him (Deuteronomy 10:12; Psalm 86:11). God's name stands for God himself as he has made himself known.

decisions.choice: compassion before this man: that the king will be kind and grant his request
decisions.reason: The word means mercy or kindness. "This man" is the king, as the sentence after it explains. Nehemiah is about to ask Artaxerxes a favor (2:1-8); before God the great king is only "this man".

decisions.choice: cupbearer: a trusted royal official who served the king's wine
decisions.reason: A cupbearer served the king his wine and guarded it from poison, so he had to be trusted and was often near the king (Genesis 40:1-13; 1 Kings 10:5). This gives Nehemiah the chance to speak to Artaxerxes (2:1).

decisions.choice: honor
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "honor" for "fear" here, since the word speaks of reverence, not terror. Literal keeps "fear".

decisions.choice: make the king kind to me
decisions.reason: Readable names "this man" as the king, as the next sentence does.
